క్లెయిమ్: భారత ఎంపీలు కొనుగోలు చేసే కార్లు, ఏసీలు, విమాన టిక్కెట్లపై జీఎస్టీ మినహాయింపుతో పాటు టోల్ టాక్స్ మినహాయింపు, ఉచిత రైలు ప్రయాణ సదుపాయాలు పొందుతారు.
ఫాక్ట్: ఎంపీలకు ఉచిత రైలు, విమాన ప్రయాణాలతో పాటు టోల్ టాక్స్ మినహాయింపు ఉన్న మాట నిజమే. కానీ, వారు కొనుగోలు చేసే కార్లు, ఏసీలుపై వారికి ఎలాంటి జీఎస్టీ మినహాయింపు లేదు. కావున, పోస్టులో చేయబడిన క్లెయిమ్ తప్పుదోవ పట్టించే విధంగా ఉంది.
ముందుగా ఎంపీలకు అందే ప్రయోజనాల గురించి పార్లమెంట్ అధికారిక వెబ్సైట్లో ఉన్న వివరాలను (ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) పరిశీలించగా, ఒక ఎంపీ తన జీవిత భాగస్వామి, బంధువులు లేదా స్నేహితులతో కలిసి దేశంలో ఎక్కడికైనా ప్రయాణించేందుకు ఏడాదికి 34 సింగిల్ విమాన టికెట్లను ఉచితంగా పొందుతారు.
అలాగే, రైలులో దేశవ్యాప్తంగా ఎక్కడి నుంచి ఎక్కడికైనా ప్రయాణించడానికి ఎంపీతో పాటు వారి జీవిత భాగస్వామి లేదా మరో వ్యక్తికి ఫస్ట్ క్లాస్ ఏసీ లేదా ఎగ్జిక్యూటివ్ క్లాస్ రైలు టికెట్లు ఉచితంగా లభిస్తాయి. వారితో పాటు వచ్చే సహాయకుడికి కూడా ఉచితంగా ఏసీ టూ-టైర్ (2-Tier) పాస్ అందుతుంది.
ఇక భారత జాతీయ రహదారుల ప్రాధికార సంస్థ (NHAI) నిబంధనల (ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) ప్రకారం, ఎంపీలు ప్రయాణం చేసే వాహనానికి జాతీయ రహదారులపై టోల్ టాక్స్ నుంచి మినహాయింపు ఉంటుంది. ఎంపీలు తమ పదవీ కాలంలో రెండు వాహనాలకు టోల్ ఫ్రీ ఫాస్టాగ్ (FASTag) లను ఉపయోగించుకోవచ్చు.
అయితే, ఎంపీలు కొనుగోలు చేసే కార్లు, ఏసీలు లేదా ఇతర వస్తువులపై జీఎస్టీ మినహాయింపు ఉంటుందనడానికి ఎలాంటి ఆధారాల్లేవు. ఎంపీల ప్రయోజనాలను వివరించే ‘The Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954’ లో గానీ, ప్రభుత్వ అధికారిక ప్రకటనల్లో గానీ ఇలాంటి వెసులుబాటు ఉన్నట్లు ఎక్కడా పేర్కొనలేదు.
చివరిగా, ఎంపీలకు ఉచిత విమాన, రైలు ప్రయాణాలు, టోల్ టాక్స్ మినహాయింపు ఉన్న మాట వాస్తవమే అయినా, వారు కొనుగోలు చేసే కార్లు, ఏసీలపై జీఎస్టీ మినహాయింపు వర్తించదు.

In late October and early November, a rumor spread that the gold covering of recently regilded equestrian bronze statues in Washington, D.C., was melting off.
U.S. President Donald Trump ordered the Arts of Peace and Arts of War statues to be regilded to mark the 250th anniversary of the foundation of the U.S. on July 4. However, the statues' renovation did not end until more than a month after that date.
The claim spread across social media, including on Facebook and Reddit. On X, a post said, "$5 million gold refurbishing is now melting off the horse statues in Washington, D.C." (archived):
The post included an image showing drip streaks at the foot of the statue, suggesting the coating was dissolving off of the statue. There was no indication the image had been fabricated or misleadingly edited. We ran the image through the artificial intelligence detector Pangram, which found no evidence of AI generation. (It is worth noting these detectors are not infallible, however.)
The Mirror US, a tabloid, republished the image showing golden drip streaks from the top of the statue's pedestal, suggesting the new coating was melting off. The Irish Star, a digital outlet, also amplified the claim.
While the National Park Service confirmed there were streaks at the foot of the statue, Snopes could not directly confirm whether the streaking really meant the gilding of the statues was melting off. For this reason, we have left the claim unrated.
"The visible streaking is associated with moisture draining through an intentionally designed system to prevent condensation from accumulating within the statues," a spokesperson for the National Park Service, which oversees the statues' conservation, told Snopes in an email. "The streaks do not indicate damage to the gilding or the recent restoration work."
We have reached out to The Gilder's Studio, which received the contract to regild the statues. We are waiting for a response.
A search on the U.S. government spending database confirmed the U.S. Department of the Interior awarded $5.1 million to The Gilder's Studio, a company in Maryland, for "THE FULL CONSERVATION AND REGILDING OF FOUR (4) MONUMENTAL EQUESTRIAN BRONZE SCULPTURES." The contract was awarded on April 21, 2026, and it ended on Sept. 30.
The goal was to cover the statues in 23.75-karat gold, according to The Washington Sun (previously known as Notus.com). One X user pointed out that the melting point of gold was "2000 degrees" (the exact melting point of gold is 1,947 degrees Farenheit, which corresponds to 1,064 degrees Celsius). The fact that it was supposedly "melting off," the person said, suggested the statues had not, in fact, been covered in gold.
Meanwhile, an X user posted a video saying the streaks were from the golden coating dissolving from the rain (archived), rather than melting.
"Like all National Park Service lands, monuments, and historic sites, the Arts of War and Arts of Peace statuary require ongoing stewardship and care to ensure they are preserved for future generations," the NPS spokesperson added in the email. "The NPS will continue to monitor the condition of the statues as part of its regular preservation and maintenance program."
Some of Trump's efforts to refurbish monuments across the U.S. capital for the 250th anniversary of the country's foundation have been thwarted. For example, Snopes covered multiple claims about the renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, including the claim that it started to peel immediately after it was repainted.

Danish minister visits India to advance green energy, trade partnership, maritime ties
Lidegaard, who visited Mumbai and New Delhi during November 2-3, described India as an increasingly important partner for Denmark
Moves by India and Denmark to take their unique Green Strategic Partnership into its next phase got a boost during Danish business minister Martin Lidegaard’s visit to the country that focused on strengthening cooperation in trade, innovation, green technologies and maritime affairs.
Lidegaard, who visited Mumbai and New Delhi during November 2-3, described India as an increasingly important partner for Denmark, economically, technologically and geopolitically. Denmark has strong skills that can support India’s ambitions in areas such as renewable energy and AI, he said.
The next phase of the bilateral Green Strategic Partnership, established in 2020, envisages enhanced cooperation in areas of shared economic and strategic interest. A new joint action plan and more high-level visits in support of the partnership are currently being prepared.
“I am in India to learn about the speed and scale of your country’s transition, strengthen our partnership and open doors for Danish companies,” said Lidegaard, who began his visit on Monday in Mumbai, where he visited APM Terminals, operated by the Danish shipping company Maersk, and discussed new economic opportunities with Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma.
In New Delhi, Lidegaard met commerce minister Piyush Goyal to discuss growing trade and economic opportunities against the backdrop of the expanding bilateral partnership and the upcoming India-European Union (EU) free trade agreement. More than 200 Danish companies operating in India employ more than 100,000 people.
He also met Union ports and shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal to discuss cooperation in green shipping, sustainable port development and green corridors. He also advanced the India-Denmark energy partnership while meeting Union renewable energy minister Pralhad Joshi and participating in the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026.
Discussions focused on expanding commercial opportunities and Denmark’s support for India’s transition to a more efficient, reliable and sustainable energy system. Denmark is the second-largest government contributor to the International Solar Alliance outside India.

Indian tourist killed after two helicopters collide near Everest base camp
- Published
An Indian tourist has died after two helicopters collided while attempting to land near the base camp of Mount Everest, two officials have confirmed to the BBC.
Verified footage of the crash showed the helicopter blades of the two aircraft clipping each other as they came into land at around 08:15 local time (02:30 GMT) in Pheriche, approximately 12km (7 miles) south of Mount Everest Base Camp.
Helicopter company Fishtail Air named the man killed in the crash as Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu.
The helicopter company said one of its vehicles was involved in the collision and that another passenger and the helicopter's captain had been injured.
The injured passengers and crew members on board were rescued and taken to Kathmandu, Fishtail Air added in a statement.
The injured passenger was a tourist from New Zealand, an official of Solukhumbu district, Bhupendra Thapa, told BBC Nepal.
The other helicopter involved was operated by Air Dynasty and had been carrying cargo, the company said.
It was operated by one crew member who sustained no injuries, it added.
A spokesman for Nepal's Civil Aviation Authority, Gyanendra Bhul, said: "It appears the accident happened when two helicopters... attempted to land at the same spot."
In the video footage of the incident, the weather conditions look clear and no strong wind effects are visible. One helicopter appears to be making a more rapid descent than the other.
Helicopters are widely used for transport in the Himalayan nation due to its challenging terrain. But its rapidly changing weather conditions and high altitude often make aviation operations hazardous.
The village of Pheriche, located on the trekking route to the summit of the world's tallest mountain, Mount Everest, is just over 4,000m (13,120ft) above sea level.
Climbing expeditions to Everest and Ama Dablam mountain are currently under way in the region, as autumn is a popular climbing season.

The Dot Max has really impressive sound for its compact size and is my overall favorite Alexa speaker, but if you're only going to use it for voice commands rather than jam sessions, you can get away with the older, cheaper model, especially if you want to buy a few to place around your home. For anyone looking for a smart display, the Echo Show 11 ($250) is the best of Amazon's newest smart displays that come designed for the updated assistant, Alexa+. The older third-generation Echo Show 8 ($150) is still a great value if you want something cheaper.
Read on to see every Alexa speaker I've tried (hint: it's all of them) and what I think after testing each one. You can also learn more about Alexa+, and we've got guides on setting up your Echo speaker, creating Alexa routines, and the best tricks an Echo Show can do.
Updated September 2026: I've updated this guide with Amazon's increased pricing that affected several models, and details about the price hike.
Comparing the Best Alexa Speakers

Honorable Mentions
While I wouldn't call these smart speakers my absolute favorites from Amazon, they have some excellent qualities that make them stand out among the vast lineup of Echo models.
The Echo Studio (2nd Gen) is the best Alexa speaker for sound quality. This is the second version of the Echo Studio to be our audiophile pick. The current version is a similar size to the old Echo (4th gen), but the musical power on this speaker is almost ridiculous. It filled my entire second floor's long great room with music, and I didn't even need to reach the highest level of volume to pull it off. Honestly, I'm almost afraid to use it at full blast. Not only was it loud, but clear and delivered a nice amount of bass, beautifully playing soft tones of Tracy Chapman's “Fast Car” and the piano riffs of “Dark Blue” by Jack's Mannequin with its three 1.5-inch drivers, plus a 3.75-inch woofer. The harmonizing of “What Is This Feeling?” by Ariana Grande and Cynthia Erivo sounded beautiful, too. If you're looking for big sound in an Alexa box, this is it. It's a similar size to the Apple HomePod, but I like the sound much better and it's cheaper, too. You'll also get a built-in smart home hub, spatial audio and Dolby Atmos, tap controls like the Echo Dot Max, and early access to Alexa+ right away.
The Echo Spot (2nd Gen) is the best Alexa speaker for bedside tables. The Echo Spot returned in 2024 after a few years of discontinuation, and it's a great little bedside companion thanks to its half-circle screen that displays the time, plus any alarms you have set are also visible under the main time. You can customize the clock with a couple of different color and face options, and the screen dims nicely when the lights are out to a gentle red that's easy to read without lighting up the room. I like asking for alarms set to my latest playlist or some lo-fi jams, and it's easy to set that up with a voice request. Unlike the Echo Shows, it doesn't have a distracting, constantly moving slideshow that would be annoying for the bedroom, nor does it display ads or have a built-in camera. (Nobody wants a rogue camera in their bedroom.) It does not have fantastic sound, but it's plenty loud for an alarm or casual listening while you get dressed in the morning.
The Echo Dot Kids (5th Gen) is the best Alexa speaker for kids. Do your kids really need their own Alexa speaker? That's up to you. This special edition of the Echo Dot is nearly identical to the fifth-gen Dot above, but it has easy-to-use parental controls that allow you to set time limits, filter explicit content, and review activity. The owl- or dragon-themed sphere comes with a year of Amazon Kids+, which includes thousands of Audible books and other special games and features. After that, you'll be charged $3 per month. Alexa can help your kids spell, play their favorite music, or—via another speaker in your house—remind them of dinner time.
More Alexa (and Alexa-Compatible) Speakers
There are a lot of Echo devices out there, and some third-party speakers that are Amazon Alexa–compatible. Here's every Alexa smart speaker we've tried and what we thought of it. Some of these speakers didn't raise in price like the models above, which might make them more appealing than before if you're looking to spend less.
Amazon Echo Dot (5th Gen) With Clock for $60: I like this version of the older Echo Dot that adds an LED clock to the front of the speaker, and was thrilled to see it in stock again last year. The LED clock can also display information like the weather when you ask Alexa questions. It's once again temporarily out of stock as of this writing, and has had spotty availability (it's out of stock right now, but Amazon says it's temporary). Still, it's a good find when it's available.
Amazon Echo Hub for $180: The Amazon Echo Hub is similar to an Echo Show, but without the speaker. Instead it's a thin device that feels a bit like a tablet, designed to be mounted on the wall (or placed on a separately purchased stand, which is how I used it) and used to control your smart home devices. It's a great choice for anyone who wants something focused on smart home control only. You can still ask Alexa questions and even play music, but the thin speakers aren't worth playing music from. But you can tell your Echo Hub to play music on a different set of speakers, and even set up default speakers to work with it. It's a great companion device if you already have a smart home setup.
Amazon Echo Pop for $40: The Echo Pop is a perfectly fine little speaker, and the cutest one in Amazon's lineup. Does it have great sound? No. It's fine enough for background tunes or if you're limited to a dorm room, but you'll get much better sound for a similar size from the Echo Dot (but you'll pay a little more, and you won't get as cute of colors)!
Amazon Echo Show 5 (3rd Gen) for $100: This smart display is another just-fine option, but it's too small to be a great display, and the included camera makes it a no for a bedside table; better to go with the above Echo Spot or an Echo Dot. This model did raise in price by $10.
Amazon Echo Show 8 (4th Gen) for $200: I usually love an Echo Show 8, but this model didn't have the same sound quality as the older model. If you're going to get one of Amazon's new displays, you're better off getting the Echo Show 11 ($220) for the same experience with a slightly larger screen (while it's a 3-inch difference, it doesn't feel that big) and better sound. This smart display raised in price by $20.
Amazon Echo Show 15 (2nd Gen) for $350: This smart display is a good display, but it clearly wants to double as a TV and isn't very good at it yet. Why Did Amazon's Prices Increase?
Amazon increased many of its prices last month for its products, affecting the Amazon Echo line as well as Kindles, Fire TV streaming sticks, and Eero routers. It's not a huge surprise after other companies have done the same this summer, claiming rising costs and chip shortages. Amazon made a similar claim, with a spokesperson blaming increased storage and memory costs. Still, it's disappointing to see and will lead to a fall sale season with prices that won't be as impressive as earlier this summer.
Amazon's Echo devices saw increases from anywhere between $20 and $100, with the larger price increases being for the Echo Shows. The following Echo speakers all faced a price increase:

What’s Alexa+?
Amazon has rolled out the new-and-improved Amazon Alexa, named Alexa+, which is built on generative AI and promises a more powerful assistant that can handle more conversational topics and requests. It's available for a free 30-day trial; after that, you either pay a $20 monthly fee or become a Prime member. Being a Prime member is the better deal, likely by design. Neither my colleagues nor I have been impressed enough by Alexa+ to say it's worth paying for on its own. I do like the updated, more conversational voice, and Alexa+ did a good job answering all kinds of questions quickly and thoughtfully. Check out our early access hands-on for everything I thought while testing.
Alexa+ has brought some changes, even for those not using it. It now requires that all voice recordings be sent to Amazon for processing, which wasn't required before. Amazon has changed its features to support this, and now all recordings with regular Alexa go to Amazon, too. There used to be a “Do Not Send Voice Recordings” privacy feature you could select to have voice requests processed locally, but it was discontinued on March 28, 2025, per an email Amazon sent to current users.
FAQs
What’s the Difference Between an Echo and an Echo Show?
A regular Echo is a smart speaker, or a speaker with microphones in it so it can hear you speak to it and respond. An Echo Show is a smart display, which has a screen and a camera to let you make video calls, stream content, and see your questions answered on a screen. Both have similar capabilities when it comes to smart home control, answering questions, and playing music, but Echo Shows have extra abilities thanks to the screen. All Echo Shows have a camera and come with a physical camera cover for privacy.
When’s the Best Time to Buy an Echo?
The best time to buy any Amazon speaker is during a major sale event like Black Friday or Amazon Prime Day, when there are often steep discounts. You'll often see the cheaper speakers for around 50 percent off, and the larger speakers see some nice sale prices too.
How and Where Should You Set Up Your Alexa?
Alexa speakers get the best use in spaces you're in often. I like setting mine up in my kitchen and living room—usually a display in the kitchen, so I can pull up a recipe or the weather while I make my morning cup of tea, and a speaker in the living room so I can play music and command the lights without a screen to distract from the TV or playing with my son. You can also set one up in the bedroom to use as an alarm clock, but make sure it's a model without a camera for the best privacy.
Ultimately, what's most important is that the speaker is somewhere it can hear your commands. Where that will be will vary based on your home, but think about where you'll be when you ask for the weather or to dim the lights, and place your speaker accordingly.
You'll set up Alexa speakers using the Alexa app, which allows you to manage multiple Alexa speakers if you own more than one through your Amazon account. Third-party speaker setup methods may vary.
Is Alexa Always Listening?
Alexa is always listening, to a certain extent. It's designed to only listen for its wake word and shouldn't be recording or processing any audio unless it hears that word. But Alexa can sometimes mishear a word and think it's the wake word, or it might hear a word similar enough to activate the speaker. If you've owned an Alexa, there have likely been times when the assistant suddenly responds when you weren't speaking to it. Once it hears the wake word (or what it believes to be the wake word), it will start listening to everything in an attempt to hear what you need and respond.
Alexa+, the latest version of Alexa, will also remain on for a little bit after you ask a question to listen for follow-up questions, no wake word required. Both Alexa and Alexa+ light up in some fashion (regular speakers will turn the light ring blue, while the displays will have a blue bar appear on the screen) to let you know the assistant is listening. Most Echo devices also have a physical mute button and will display a red light or red bar to let you know when the mute is activated.
How Do You Remove Ads and Spam From an Echo Show?
If you're using an Echo Show device, you've likely noticed there is a ton of default content the device will show you. Sports scores! Local news! A recipe you might be interested in! It makes the device exhausting and annoying to be near.
Here's how you can control what you see:
- Swipe down from the top of your Echo Show to pull up the menu, and select Settings.
- In the Settings menu, choose Home Content.
- There are more than 40 options you can toggle on and off on this menu, and you should remove as many as you can that you don't use. I usually remove all but weather forecasts and recently played audio.
While you're able to turn off interest-based ads from third-party skills (this is under Alexa Privacy in the Settings menu), it won't stop all ads. The only setting that is ad-free is choosing Photo Display mode, which can use either Amazon's included library of photos or your own. The downside is that it turns it into a digital photo frame, so you won't even see a clock or features like widgets.
Can I Have My Alexa Requests Locally Processed, or Do They Have to Go to the Cloud?
There used to be a privacy feature called Do Not Send Voice Recordings that let you have all your voice requests processed locally on your Alexa device instead of being sent to Amazon's cloud storage. That feature was killed in March 2025 to support Alexa+, and even if you continue to use the old Alexa, you don't have access to that feature any longer.
How Does WIRED Select Smart Speakers to Test? How Are These Speakers Tested?
For this guide, we specifically test speakers that are compatible with Amazon Alexa. It's a big limitation and narrows down the options significantly, especially compared to speaker options you'll see in our other guides like the Best Bluetooth Speakers. That's mainly Amazon's own ecosystem of speakers, and while there are third-party options, the best options tend to be of Amazon's own design to work with its own voice assistant.
Each speaker gets installed in a tester's home for day-to-day use, to see how the microphone performs, how the speaker sounds with different types of music, how well the smart home control features work with compatible devices such as smart lights and video doorbells, and to test other features as necessary (e.g., streaming features on smart displays).
How Does WIRED Get Models? What Does WIRED Do After Testing Them?
We acquire review units usually as a press sample, though we will also independently purchase samples if need be. All review units in this guide were provided as press samples with no obligation to cover or promises for what that coverage would be.
After testing, we keep most of our picks either installed for long-term testing in our homes or in storage to compare against updated models and new speakers that come out. If the sample becomes irrelevant or unnecessary to keep, we donate it locally.

The battle for control of the US Congress is under way, and Republicans have reason to be nervous.
As millions of Americans head to polling stations on November 3, the latest surveys point to a difficult electoral environment for President Donald Trump's Republican Party, with Democrats building a substantial lead in the national congressional preference polls and gaining ground in several traditionally Republican states.
The elections are shaping up as a referendum on Trump's second presidency, with voters weighing the administration's handling of the economy, the cost of living, immigration, tariffs and the war involving Iran.
All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships are being contested.
For Democrats, the midterms offer an opportunity to turn dissatisfaction with the White House into control of Congress. For Republicans, the challenge is to prevent a midterm backlash from becoming a decisive repudiation of Trump's political agenda.
All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships are being contested.
The outcome will determine not only who controls the legislative agenda for the remaining two years of Trump's presidency but also how much political leverage the president retains heading into the 2028 presidential election.
The numbers
The national polling picture has shifted considerably in the Democrats' favour in the final stretch of the campaign. 
A polling aggregation updated on November 3 puts the Democratic advantage on the generic congressional ballot at approximately 8.4 percentage points.
The figures represent national preferences for congressional elections, rather than predictions of individual seat outcomes. Nevertheless, a Democratic lead of this magnitude is significant, particularly given how narrow the Republican majority in the House is.
An earlier RealClearPolling average, cited by Al Jazeera on October 31, had Democrats ahead 51.4% to 43.2%, an 8.2-point advantage. An Economist/YouGov survey also found that 44% of registered voters expected Democrats to control the House after the election, against 31% who expected Republicans to retain it.
The Senate picture was less settled in that survey: 39% expected Democrats to win control, while 36% anticipated a Republican majority.
Perhaps the most consequential development is the latest forecast from election analyst Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin. Its final November 3 forecast says a Democratic House majority now looks almost certain and that Democrats have also moved into a strong position to capture the Senate.
The model's polling averages show Democrats ahead in practically every major Senate battleground, including Texas, Ohio, Michigan, Maine and Iowa. Even states that Republicans would ordinarily expect to defend comfortably have become competitive.
The figures are especially striking in Texas, Ohio and Kansas, where Democrats are attempting to break through in states that have traditionally leaned Republican in federal elections.
However, polls are not predictions. A lead of three or four percentage points can disappear within the margin of error, and turnout, undecided voters and differences between likely-voter and registered-voter samples could still change the outcome.
Why the Democrats believe a blue wave is possible
Historically, the party occupying the White House tends to lose ground in midterm elections. The president's party has lost House seats in 18 of the last 20 midterm elections over the past 80 years, making the November vote particularly uncomfortable for Trump.
Historically, the president’s party often loses congressional seats in these elections
But this election is also being shaped by a combination of issues that Democrats believe have created an unusually difficult environment for Republicans.
- The economy and cost of living: Affordability has emerged as a central campaign issue. Voters are concerned about everyday expenses, energy prices, healthcare costs and the pressure on household budgets. Republicans are facing questions about whether Trump's economic policies have delivered the relief promised during the 2024 presidential campaign. Democrats have sought to connect tariffs and the Iran war to higher costs for consumers, farmers and businesses. In Iowa, for instance, the impact of tariffs and the rising cost of diesel and fertiliser have become central to the campaign. Rural voters, traditionally an important Republican constituency, are being targeted by Democrats with an affordability message.
- The Iran war: The war involving Iran has become another major political vulnerability for the administration. Republicans are facing criticism over its economic consequences, particularly energy prices and the wider uncertainty surrounding American military involvement. The issue has also created a difficult balancing act for GOP candidates who must defend the president's foreign policy while attempting to keep the focus on domestic concerns.
- Trump's approval ratings: Trump's popularity is another major concern for Republicans. The New York Times polling average put his approval rating at approximately 37% ahead of Election Day. Democrats have sought to turn dissatisfaction with the president into votes against Republican candidates, even in constituencies that Trump won comfortably in 2024.
- Early voting and turnout: More than 43 million Americans had already voted early, either in person or through returned mail ballots, five days before Election Day, according to an Associated Press analysis. That was nearly 10 million more than at the equivalent stage before the 2022 midterms. Texas had recorded more than 6.3 million early ballots by October 28, against 4.2 million at the corresponding stage in 2022 — an increase of around 50%. Georgia had also crossed 2.5 million early ballots by October 30, surpassing its 2022 early-voting figure of 2.3 million. The numbers indicate heightened electoral engagement, although early voting figures alone cannot establish which party will benefit.
Economy, democracy, healthcare, education and immigration are the top concerns of US voters.
The House:  Republicans' biggest vulnerability
The party entered the election with 219 seats against the Democrats' 214, with two vacancies. Democrats therefore need a net gain of just four seats to secure a majority.
The House balance at 219 Republicans to 214 Democrats, with two vacancies
That relatively small hurdle has made dozens of districts competitive, including several that Trump carried in 2024.
The challenge for Republicans is compounded by the fact that the president's party generally faces a midterm disadvantage. Democrats, meanwhile, have been encouraged by the national polling advantage and their performance in a number of special elections.
The Cook Political Report and other election forecasters have identified a broad collection of Republican-held seats that could become vulnerable.
Among the most important House contests are:
- NEW YORK Republican Congressman Mike Lawler faces Democrat Cait Conley in New York's 17th Congressional District. The constituency is particularly important because it is among the few Republican-held districts that Kamala Harris carried in the 2024 presidential election. Lawler has built his political identity around appealing to moderate voters, but the national political environment could make his re-election considerably more difficult. Conley is attempting to capitalise on dissatisfaction with Trump and turn the district's Democratic lean in the presidential election into a congressional victory. The latest polling aggregation puts Conley approximately two percentage points ahead, making this one of the most closely watched Republican-held seats.
- IOWA Iowa's first congressional district is another important test of whether Democrats can win back voters in traditionally Republican territory. Republican Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks faces Democrat Christina Bohannan, who has unsuccessfully challenged her in previous elections. The contest has become more competitive amid concerns about tariffs, farm costs and the wider economic outlook. Democrats have also invested heavily in the district. Reuters reported that they had spent approximately $11 million compared with $7 million by Republicans. The latest polling aggregation showed Bohannan with a substantial lead, although the district's Republican lean and the history of Miller-Meeks' victories make this a race worth watching closely.
- TEXAS Texas has become a particularly important battleground because of the Republican effort to redraw congressional boundaries to improve the party's chances of retaining its House majority. Republicans hoped the redistricting exercise would create additional favourable seats. But Democrats are attempting to turn the backlash against the process into an electoral advantage. Several Texas districts are now being closely monitored, including the 9th District, where the polling aggregation shows Democrat Alex Mealer narrowly ahead of the Republican incumbent. The 15th District is another contest to watch, with Republican Monica De La Cruz facing a challenge from Democrat Bobby Pulido. The outcome will help establish whether Republican efforts to reshape congressional boundaries have delivered the expected advantage.
Other House races to watch
- Arizona's 1st District: Democrat Amish Shah is challenging Republican Jay Feely in a competitive open-seat contest. Shah's campaign has attracted significant outside spending, and the latest polling aggregation gives him a four-point advantage.
- Florida's 22nd District: Democrat Pia Dandiya is challenging Republican Casey Askar in a seat that has been rated a toss-up by major election forecasters.
- Pennsylvania's 7th District: Republican Ryan Mackenzie faces Democrat Ryan Crosswell in another closely watched contest.
- Michigan's 10th District: Democrat Christina Hines and Republican Michael Bouchard are competing for an open seat after John James entered the gubernatorial race.
- Montana's 1st District: Democrat Sam Forstag is attempting to unseat Republican Aaron Flint in a district Trump won comfortably in 2024.
- New Jersey's 7th District: Democrat Rebecca Bennett is challenging Republican Tom Kean Jr., who has faced criticism over his absence from congressional votes.
These contests are part of a much larger battle. CBS News identified 42 House races that could determine which party controls the chamber.
Senate: Could Democrats pull off an even bigger upset?
The Senate battle is more complicated.
Republicans currently hold 53 seats against the Democrats' 47. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to reach a majority, assuming the existing chamber alignment.
The Senate is arguably the more consequential prize in terms of appointments and the long-term balance of power in Washington.
This is a considerably more difficult proposition than winning the House because Republicans are defending seats in a number of states Trump carried by comfortable margins in 2024. But the latest surveys have given Democrats fresh hope.
Five Senate contests deserve particular attention.
1. Texas: James Talarico's opportunity to make history
Texas is emerging as one of the biggest potential Democratic breakthroughs of the election.
Democrat James Talarico is challenging Republican Ken Paxton, the state's attorney general, for a Senate seat.
Paxton defeated incumbent Republican Senator John Cornyn in the GOP primary, but his nomination has raised questions about whether Republicans have selected the strongest possible candidate for a general election contest.
His history of personal and political controversies has given Democrats an opening.
Talarico, a state representative and former teacher, has sought to build a campaign around economic issues, healthcare and a broader appeal to voters dissatisfied with the political establishment.
The November 1 New York Times/Siena poll put Talarico ahead 50% to 43%.
A polling average also showed him leading by approximately three points. A Democratic victory would be particularly significant: the party has not won a Texas Senate election since 1988.
2. Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed takes on Mike Rogers
Michigan is another state where Democrats are hoping to make a significant gain.
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is challenging Republican Mike Rogers for an open Senate seat following the retirement of Senator Gary Peters.
El-Sayed, a progressive former Michigan health official, won a divisive Democratic primary against a more moderate opponent.
Rogers, a former congressman, is attempting to return to the Senate after losing his previous election battle against Elissa Slotkin.
The latest New York Times/Siena survey gave El-Sayed a commanding 53%-42% lead.
This is particularly important because Michigan is a major battleground state where the Democratic candidate's performance could help establish whether the party's national polling advantage is translating into votes.
3. Ohio: Sherrod Brown attempts a comeback
Former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown is attempting to reclaim his seat after losing his re-election bid in 2024.
He faces Republican Senator Jon Husted, who was appointed to the seat vacated by JD Vance after Vance became vice-president.
Brown has sought to position himself as a champion of working-class voters, an important constituency in a state that has moved increasingly towards Republicans in recent elections.
His campaign is attempting to make the election about manufacturing jobs, economic insecurity and the cost of living.
The New York Times/Siena poll put Brown ahead 49%-44%, suggesting that Ohio could become one of the biggest Democratic surprises of the night.
4. Maine: Susan Collins faces a serious challenge
Republican Senator Susan Collins is fighting to retain her seat against Democrat Troy Jackson.
Collins has survived several difficult election campaigns and has often benefited from her ability to attract support beyond the Republican base.
But the political environment is different this time. Maine voted for Kamala Harris in 2024, and Democrats believe the state's electorate could turn against Republicans in the midterms.
The November 1 Siena poll showed Jackson leading Collins 51%-45%.
A Democratic victory here would be particularly consequential because Collins has been a prominent Republican figure in the Senate for decades.
5. Alaska: Mary Peltola threatens another Republican seat
Former Democratic Congresswoman Mary Peltola is challenging Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska.
Alaska is not an obvious Democratic pickup opportunity. The state has a strong Republican voting history and has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 2008.
But Peltola has demonstrated an ability to appeal to voters beyond the traditional Democratic base.
The latest Siena poll showed her leading Sullivan 48%-46%.
Even a narrow victory would be a major breakthrough for Democrats and could prove decisive in the battle for Senate control.
Other Senate contests that could decide control
| State | Democratic candidate | Republican candidate | Latest polling picture | 
| Kansas | Adam Hamilton | Roger Marshall | Hamilton +5 | 
| Iowa | Josh Turek | Ashley Hinson | Turek +1 | 
| Georgia | Jon Ossoff | Mike Collins | Ossoff +9.2 | 
| North Carolina | Roy Cooper | Michael Whatley | Cooper +10.9 | 
| New Hampshire | Chris Pappas | John Sununu | Pappas +7.3 | 
| Nebraska | Independent/Democratic-aligned candidate | Pete Ricketts | Ricketts +0.9 | 
Kansas is especially interesting. Democrat Adam Hamilton is attempting to become the first Democrat to win a Senate election in the state since 1932.
The race against Republican Senator Roger Marshall has become competitive because of concerns over affordability, energy costs and the Iran war.
Georgia, meanwhile, is a test of whether Republicans can unseat Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff. Republican Mike Collins is challenging him, but the latest polling averages suggest Ossoff has a substantial advantage.
North Carolina is another important opportunity for Democrats. Former governor Roy Cooper is running against Republican Michael Whatley in an open-seat contest. Cooper's popularity and statewide political experience have made him a formidable challenger.
Together, these races could determine whether Democrats can overcome the unfavourable Senate map and take control of the chamber.
Governor races: Democrats eye a historic breakthrough
While congressional control is the biggest national prize, the gubernatorial contests could produce a political realignment of their own.
A total of 36 states are electing governors, representing approximately 80% of the US population. Nineteen of those contests involve open seats.
Gubernatorial contests could produce a political realignment of their own.
Democrats are hoping to win control of a majority of governors' offices for the first time in two decades. Their last such breakthrough came in 2006, when they flipped six governorships during the midterm elections of George W Bush's presidency.
The most closely watched races include:
1. Ohio: Vivek Ramaswamy vs Amy Acton
This is arguably the most closely watched gubernatorial contest from an Indian-American perspective.
Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, backed by Trump, is running against Democrat Amy Acton, the former Ohio health director.
Ramaswamy entered the campaign with considerable national visibility, having previously contested the 2024 Republican presidential nomination and later worked with the Trump administration's Department of Government Efficiency initiative.
Vivek Ramaswamy entered the campaign with considerable national visibility
Acton, meanwhile, is seeking to make the race a referendum on Republican leadership in the state.
The latest New York Times/Siena survey put Acton ahead 49%-43%. Another November 1 survey by Survey 160 showed her leading 51%-44%.
The polling average on November 2 gave Acton a lead of approximately 3.8 points.
The campaign has also been marred by controversy over a political advertisement involving Acton's family, which attracted criticism from both Democrats and some prominent Republicans.
A Democratic victory would be a significant setback for Trump, who has publicly backed Ramaswamy.
2. Texas: Gina Hinojosa vs Greg Abbott
Democrat Gina Hinojosa is mounting a challenge to Republican Governor Greg Abbott, who is seeking another term.
No Democrat has won a statewide election in Texas since 1994, making the contest particularly significant.
Hinojosa has sought to make affordability, healthcare and economic opportunity central to her campaign.
The New York Times/Siena survey showed her narrowly ahead 48%-47%, putting Abbott under unusual pressure in a state where Republicans have dominated statewide politics for decades.
3. Georgia: An opening for Democrats
Georgia has not elected a Democratic governor since 1998.
The open-seat contest has therefore attracted considerable national attention, with Democrats believing that the wider political climate could help them overcome the state's Republican lean.
4. Iowa and Alaska: Testing Republican strongholds
Both states have competitive open-seat gubernatorial contests.
In Iowa, Democrat Rob Sand is challenging Republican Zach Lahn, while in Alaska Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is facing Republican Bernadette Wilson.
The Siena survey gave the Democratic candidates leads of 51%-43% and 54%-46%, respectively.
5. Florida: Can Democrats make another breakthrough?
Republican Byron Donalds, a prominent Trump ally, is challenging Democrat David Jolly.
Florida has become increasingly Republican in recent elections, but Democrats believe the economic environment could make the contest more competitive than expected.
Indian-Americans in the fray: A growing political footprint
The 2026 elections are also important for the Indian-American community, with candidates of Indian origin contesting positions ranging from the US House of Representatives to governorships, attorney-general offices and local government.

The growing presence of Indian-Americans in American politics reflects a broader shift in the country's political landscape. Their participation is no longer confined to a handful of congressional constituencies. Candidates are competing in states across the country, representing both major political parties.
Among the prominent candidates are Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam, all seeking another term in Congress.
Republican Vivek Ramaswamy is the most high-profile Indian-origin candidate contesting a gubernatorial election.
Other Indian-origin candidates to watch
The election also features several Indian-American candidates seeking to expand their political representation beyond the traditional congressional contests.
- Amish Shah — Arizona: The Democrat and former Arizona state legislator is challenging Republican Jay Feely in the 1st Congressional District. The race has attracted significant outside spending and could become an important Democratic pickup.
- Pia Dandiya — Florida: Dandiya is contesting Florida's 22nd Congressional District against Republican Casey Askar. The race has been rated a toss-up by several election forecasters.
- Saritha Komatireddy — New York: The Republican candidate is challenging Democratic Attorney General Letitia James. A former federal prosecutor, Komatireddy has worked on national security and organised-crime cases. Polls have shown James with a lead.
- Nithya Raman — Los Angeles: The Indian-origin Los Angeles City Council member is challenging incumbent Mayor Karen Bass. Her campaign adds another prominent South Asian face to the American political contest.
- Pooja Sethi — Texas: A Democrat contesting Texas House District 47, Sethi is a lawyer who previously served as chief of staff in the Texas Legislature.
- Sandeep Srivastava — Texas: Srivastava is challenging Republican Matt Shaheen in Texas House District 66. He previously contested a congressional election in 2024.
There are also Indian-origin candidates contesting other state-level positions and legislative seats, reflecting the expanding reach of the community in American politics.
Why the outcome matters
The midterms are not just about which party controls Congress. They could determine the political trajectory of Trump's remaining two years in office.
A Democratic takeover of the House would give the opposition control over committees, investigations, legislative priorities and congressional oversight.
It could also complicate the administration's ability to pass major legislation, particularly on immigration, taxation, federal spending and foreign policy.
The midterms  determine the political trajectory of Trump's remaining two years in office.
A Democratic Senate majority would have even greater consequences. It could influence confirmations of senior administration officials and federal judges, while giving Democrats control over a chamber that has been central to Trump's legislative agenda.
A Republican victory, on the other hand, would allow the president to continue governing with support from both chambers and would weaken the argument that voters have rejected his second-term agenda.
There is also a longer-term political calculation.

Potential Democratic presidential contenders, including governors and senators, will be closely watched. Strong performances could establish them as credible candidates for 2028, while Republican candidates will be judged on their ability to maintain Trump's coalition.
The gubernatorial elections are particularly important because state governors exercise considerable authority over election administration, a matter likely to become increasingly significant as the country approaches the next presidential election.
What happens next?
Polling stations are opening across the country on November 3 (from 3.30pm IST) with voting hours varying by state and local jurisdiction.
The first results will emerge after polling closes in individual states. However, the Senate and House contests are likely to produce different timelines for a clear picture, particularly where margins are narrow and mail ballots take longer to process.
For Indian audiences, the first substantial results are expected to emerge during the morning and afternoon of November 4, India time.
The biggest immediate indicators will be the early returns from competitive House districts, followed by the Senate battlegrounds in states such as Texas, Ohio, Michigan, Maine and Iowa.
A Democratic victory in the House is increasingly anticipated by polling models. The real question is whether the party can go further and capture the Senate as well.
For Trump, the stakes are considerable. A midterm defeat would not remove him from office, but it could transform the remainder of his presidency into a prolonged battle with an opposition-controlled Congress. For Democrats, the election offers an opportunity to turn public dissatisfaction into institutional power. And for Indian-Americans, it offers another chance to establish that their political presence in the United States is becoming increasingly difficult to overlook.

- Meanwhile, the physical double-sided map/poster will cost $0.99 on the Rockstar Store shortly after the game's launch.

Rockstar has announced in its latest Newswire blog that it will offer the GTA 6 Leonida map and the cover art poster as free digital downloads on its official website starting November 19, 2026. Players can download and print both the cover art and map themselves and keep them as collectibles. But what about the physical map?
According to Rockstar’s latest Newswire blog, published on November 3, 2026, players can buy the double-sided physical poster, featuring the cover art and full map, for $0.99 or get it for free with any purchase from the Rockstar Store, shortly after the game’s launch. | GTA 6 Collectible | Price | Release Date |

| Grand Theft Auto VI Cover Art Poster | Free (Digital download) | November 19, 2026 |

Shock and anger in India after eight-year-old beats six-year-old in classroom
- Published
Warning: Some details in this story could be distressing for some readers.
There has been shock and anger in India over video footage from the CCTV of a school that shows an eight-year-old boy brutally beating a six-year-old girl.
The girl, who was seriously injured, is recovering in hospital and is now out of danger but remains traumatised by the assault in Haryana state, her family has said.
Police say they have registered a case and the eight-year-old has been sent to a home for juvenile offenders where he is undergoing psychiatric evaluation.
The school principal and two other teachers have been suspended for suspected negligence, police say.
The incident that took place in a government school in Panchkula in the northern state of Haryana on 28 October came to light at the weekend after the CCTV footage went viral on social media.
The motive of the boy is not known.
The horrific assault has sent shock waves through the country. Many people expressed anguish over the little girl's injuries - and the brutality displayed by the boy.
Police say the eight-year-old, who is studying in third grade, told the girl that her father was waiting for her in a classroom where he assaulted her.
The family of the girl, who studies in kindergarten, reached the school after being informed by an auto-rickshaw driver that he had gone to pick her up but could not find her.
"When the girl was not found even after school ended, we went in to look for her. No one there knew where she was," her father told BBC Punjabi.
He said the boy who assaulted his daughter told him that she was in a classroom upstairs, where he found his seriously injured daughter.
"When I saw her, I almost screamed. Looking at her condition, I thought they'd killed my daughter. If a child isn't safe in school, then where will she be safe?"
The girl was initially taken to a local hospital but later moved to the multi-speciality PGIMER hospital in the nearby city of Chandigarh.
A statement from PGIMER said the six-year-old girl was "brought to the hospital with critical injuries".
She is under the care of a multidisciplinary team of specialists, which is closely monitoring her condition and providing all necessary medical attention, the hospital said.
"The circumstances involving this little child are deeply concerning. We want to ensure that she receives the best possible medical care, along with all the support and comfort she needs," the statement quoted hospital director Vivek Lal as saying.
The hospital later shared a photo of Dr Lal with the girl sitting in her father's lap and smiling.
In a video statement on Saturday, senior police official Aditi Singh said they had registered an FIR (first information report) against the school management for "negligence" and were investigating what happened.
"The boy is being evaluated by mental experts under the Juvenile Justice Act and further action will be taken accordingly," she added.
Under Indian law, an eight-year-old cannot be punished or sent to jail so the child has been sent to an observation home run by the Juvenile Justice Board, another senior police official Amarinder Singh said.
The emphasis in cases involving minors is on reformation and counselling, he added.
Meanwhile, the Haryana state government has formed a committee to investigate what happened and whether there was any negligence in the case.

An analysis of data from wearables, such as daily steps and minutes of physical activity, showed a consistent pattern where one's genetic risk was less strongly linked to depression severity among more active adults.
"Depression is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide, so understanding how we might reduce its burden is important," author Denver Brown, assistant professor in the school of health sciences at Kansas State University, US, said.
"As we move toward more personalised medicine, understanding a patient's genetic risk could help inform conversations about lifestyle, including the potential role of physical activity in helping prevent depression or manage its symptoms," Brown said.
Adding physical activity to a daily routine could therefore be especially beneficial for individuals with a genetic predisposition to depression, potentially helping reduce their risk and ease their symptom burden, the researchers said.
The study, published in the journal Nature Mental Health, analysed data from 23,517 participants of the All of Us Research Program, a nationwide effort in the U.S. to better understand how differences in biology, lifestyle and environment influence health.
"... these findings suggest that genetic and behavioural factors contribute largely independently to MDD (major depressive disorder) onset but interact in shaping symptom expression, highlighting PA (physical activity) as a potential modifier of genetic vulnerability in depression and a potential target for precision mental health interventions," the authors wrote.
The researchers analysed survey responses, electronic health records, genetic data and long-term physical activity data from Fitbit devices.
At the neurobiological level, physical activity enhances neuroplasticity by supporting synaptic plasticity and hippocampal function -- the systems are often dysregulated in depression and implicated in genetic vulnerability pathways, they said.
Exercise also regulates inflammation and improves immune signalling, which the team said is relevant, given growing evidence linking genetic risk for depression to immune and inflammatory signalling.
Further, the researchers said being physically active influences stress reactivity, potentially reducing the impact of genetically mediated stress sensitivity on depressive symptoms.

Manchester United 3-2 Roma: Bruno Fernandes claims players don't need to save Michael Carrick's job after first win in 10 games
Bruno Fernandes feels Manchester United players didn't need to save Michael Carrick's job in their 3-2 comeback win over Roma; Carrick's side avoided going ten games without a win for the first time in over four decades
Tuesday 3 November 2026 23:47, UK
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has come out in support of head coach Michael Carrick, but reiterated that the players didn't need to save his job in their 3-2 comeback win against Roma.
United and Carrick looked dead and buried within the first 18 minutes as the Italian side took a two-goal lead in the early exchanges.
It prompted boos and protests from supporters, who threw tennis balls onto the pitch, but the Red Devils turned things around as a Fernandes penalty and a late Matheus Cunha double gave them their first win in 54 days.
The spirit shown in the performance suggested at least some on-pitch support for Carrick, whose tenure appeared to have been hanging on by a thread ever since the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.
Fernandes was named on the bench for that game after publicly questioning the tactics in a sobering 4-1 defeat to Como four days prior. His words after Roma, though, were a lot more defiant than accusatory.
- Man Utd 3-2 Roma: Match report and reaction

"We don't need to save anyone's job," Fernandes told Amazon Prime post-match.
"We've been working so hard to get out of this situation altogether. It's been tough. There's been a lot of speculation in the media, a lot of lies around many things that have happened in this club. Between me and the manager, that we had to clear the air. Nothing like that happened.
"The manager took a decision of putting myself on the bench because I wasn't performing at that level. Everyone felt that it was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right.
"The manager is the one who makes the decisions. I have to accept them, I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, in the staff and every player that is in this club. It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me. It should be [a turning point]."
Carrick himself similarly played down suggestions that the turnaround could've helped his cause, saying "it's a win for us as a football club," when asked how the result could change the narrative.
"I think we've shown a lot of character as a group to weather what we've had to. You find out a lot about each other, the players will find out things about me. I certainly do about them and their character and what it means to them and what they're prepared to put in."
The win, and the nature of it, feels very reminiscent of a 2018 3-2 win over Newcastle during Jose Mourinho's time at the club. Two early goals stunned the home side, who were already under immense pressure for their poor start to the season.
In the second half, a response. A player who reportedly had his issues with Mourinho, Anthony Martial, found the net en route to a comeback which was secured by a severely underperforming South American in Alexis Sanchez.
Tonight, the role of Mourinho was played by Carrick. The role of Martial you could argue was played by Fernandes, regardless of how he feels his comments following Como were perceived. And the role of Sanchez was bettered by Cunha's heroics.
Did it save Mourinho his job? Ultimately, it didn't. He was sacked by December that year, but maybe it gave him a bit more time at the helm.
In the ten games prior to the Newcastle win, Mourinho's United had only won three times. In the 13 after, they picked up five, plus draws against Chelsea and Arsenal that weren't to be scoffed at. The issue was, the expectations at United were higher in 2018, and that return wasn't cutting it.
In reality, if Carrick managed a run of five wins, four draws and four defeats over the next 13 games, he probably isn't shown the door and is given more time to build on the project. Especially if there are some disagreements from the higher-ups on who should be the man to replace him if they went down that route.
There is just one variable that will make or break things for Carrick. Can he go back-to-back? If his United side can beat Aston Villa on Sunday, it could be the statement the former midfielder needs to earn him more time.
Unai Emery is widely regarded as the best boss in the Premier League. If Carrick is sacked, many United fans would be begging to see him take the hot seat. But, with the spirit and belief in the dressing room higher than it has been in two months following Tuesday's spectacular comeback, Carrick has a chance to get one over on Emery and leave a final impression on his bosses before the international break.
It won't be until Sunday evening, when the final whistle is blown at Old Trafford, that we will truly know whether or not Carrick's men saved his job, rather appropriately, in Fergie time.

A 24-year-old woman who died after the New York City Marathon on Sunday was suffering from a rare side effect of exercise called rhabdomyolysis, her family said.
Rachel Apa, an experienced D1 field hockey athlete who spent months training for the race, collapsed near mile 24 in Central Park and was taken by ambulance to the hospital, her father told The New York Times.
Apa was a product manager for an electronic manufacturing company. Earlier this year, she posted on LinkedIn that she was running the marathon to raise money for the Parkinson's Foundation, in honor of her grandfather.
The New York Road Runners, the group that organizes the marathon, and Apa's family did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Business Insider.
Rhabdomyolysis, known as rhabdo, is a risk of extensive strenuous exercise caused by muscle tissue breaking down and overloading the kidneys.
Without prompt medical treatment, it can be life-threatening. Here's what to know about rhabdo, including the symptoms to look out for and how to prevent it.
What is rhabdomyolysis and what causes it?
Rhabdomyolysis can occur after severe muscle injury or intense exertion. As damaged muscle tissue breaks down, it releases compounds into the bloodstream that the kidneys typically filter out.
In rare cases, those byproducts can overwhelm the kidneys and lead to kidney damage or acute kidney failure.
About 26,000 cases of rhabdo are reported in the US each year, research suggests.
Anyone can suffer from rhabdo, but factors like hot environments and dehydration can increase the risk, according to Cleveland Clinic.
While it's generally not common, cases of rhabdo are often caused by high-intensity exercise or long endurance sessions without rest. For instance, research has previously linked cases of rhabdo to marathons (particularly during high temperatures) and vigorous spin classes.
It's also increasingly a concern for the military, which is working to spot rhabdo in troops more quickly.
What are the symptoms of rhabdo?
Symptoms of rhabdo include fatigue, muscle cramps or unexpected pain, and dark-colored urine, which can show up hours or days after exercise, according to the CDC.
Rhabdo can be diagnosed with a blood test and treated with IV fluids to help flush out the waste products.
To prevent rhabdo, avoid pushing too hard during exercise, take breaks as needed, and drink plenty of water, especially in hot, humid weather.

When the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, visited India for the second time this year, headlines concentrated on who he met and where he went.
The fact that Rubio bypassed New Delhi and did not meet the prime minister, Narendra Modi, during his trip last week, and instead traveled to the financial capital, Mumbai, where he met India’s foreign minister, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar (pictured top with Rubio), and business leaders, did not go unnoticed. Nor did his decision to travel to Jamnagar, the small Gujarati town that is home to Reliance Industries’ colossal oil refinery complex.
Bilateral ties between the two countries have come under strain under the second Trump administration, particularly over tariffs and India’s purchase of Russian oil. Yet, Rubio’s return to India just five months after his first visit as secretary of state signals that the country remains useful for president Donald Trump’s ambitions after all.
As director of the South Asia Program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, Milan Vaishnav has spent a decade tracking India’s place in the world, particularly its ties with the US. Vaishnav has described Trump 2.0 as “unbound” marking a new era in India-US relations.
Tracking foreign affairs, he told me, is a minefield right now. From the White House’s transactional approach to global alliances, ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and consequential elections around the world, politics is changing at a pace that means all predictions are off the table. “I think anyone who tells you they know exactly what is going on and how it fits into their neat theory of the world is lying to you,” says Vaishnav.
I asked him about the many confusing aspects of the US-India relationship, from the hostile political rhetoric to the US embrace of Pakistan, as well as Rubio’s latest visit.
Trump the deal-maker
Ahead of Rubio’s visit, several commentators noted the secretary of state’s “unusual” itinerary. Vaishnav thought the pre-visit chatter about Rubio skipping Delhi to visit Mumbai and Jamnagar was overblown. “Not every bilateral meeting has to take place in a national capital,” he says.
But that doesn’t mean it wasn’t noteworthy. “I do think the choice of venues was intentional. This administration and, particularly, this president, sees foreign policy through the lens of ‘deal-making’. And if you’re trying to drum up business deals, what better place to visit than Mumbai?” he says.
The Jamnagar visit, where Rubio met Mukesh Ambani, the chair of Reliance, also indicates some politicking. “At a time when petrol prices are extremely high in the United States and are likely to be a major issue in the 3 November midterm elections, the administration wants to show that it is doing everything it can to bring them down. India is a major consumer of oil, but it is also a major exporter of refined petroleum products,” says Vaishnav. “One of Rubio’s objectives was to encourage Reliance and, by extension, India to process more Venezuelan crude [oil],” he added.
While this could present an opportunity for India to advance relations, it’s not a given: the US president remains, after all – and to put it lightly – mercurial.
“The biggest plot twist for me has been the Trump administration’s embrace of Pakistan after the May 2025 conflict with India,” says Vaishnav. Pakistan’s standing in Washington had eroded over the years, especially under Joe Biden, who left office without ever having made a presidential phone call to his counterpart in Pakistan. “Many officials in Congress had grown exhausted with Pakistan’s double game, speaking the language of partnership on the one hand while undermining US interests on the other,” says Vaishnav.
But, after coming to power the second time, Trump thanked the country for its help in nabbing a suspect linked to a 2021 bombing in Afghanistan that killed 13 US service members. This reversal in Pakistan’s fortunes gathered pace after the May conflict with India, which Trump took credit for ending. In June, he welcomed Asim Munir, Pakistan’s army chief, to the White House, after Munir called for the president to be nominated for the Nobel peace prize.
“I chalk up the reversal to a few factors: Trump’s well-known strongman envy, Pakistan’s savvy diplomacy, and the prospect of energy and crypto deals involving members of Trump’s inner circle,” says Vaishnav. For him, it isyet another demonstration of how much weight Trump places on deals, transactions and short-term wins. “For New Delhi, this means Modi’s personal rapport with Trump and 25 years of investment in the bilateral relationship offer no guarantee against a 180-degree reversal in US policy,” he adds.
In a recent piece, Vaishnav’s colleague Sameer Lalwani pointed out that the US relationship with India remains more resilient than the political rhetoric may suggest with quiet, but nonetheless strategic, progress being made.
As Lalwani points out, bilateral trade reached a record high between India and the US in 2025; nearly $68bn worth of AI infrastructure investment in India has been pledged by US technology companies; and the two countries have carried out record number of joint military exercises this year.
The way forward
Despite these wins, in terms of future bilateral relations, “there are at least three reasons for caution,” warns Vaishnav. First, he points to the onslaught of US actions that have dented Indian interests. Trump had imposed a punitive 50% tariff on India in 2025, which was reduced to 18% earlier this year, but without a comprehensive trade deal being reached. Second, on immigration, the White House’s H-1B visa and green card restrictions have disproportionately affected Indian workers in Silicon Valley.
“This has created a real trust deficit on the Indian side, and with good reason,” says Vaishnav. The frustration was on display earlier this month, when New Delhi branded remarks made by the US vice-president, JD Vance, about Indian professionals as “deeply offensive”. Furthermore, Vaishnav argues that while governments and private sector firms might be great at making announcements, they’re not always a guarantee of delivery.
His final caution is how political tensions can have a chilling effect. The trade negotiations offer a telling example: in January, the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, blamed the lack of a trade deal on Modi’s failure to phone Trump, a characterisation that New Delhi has disputed. Vaishnav says: “Much of the progress we are seeing is the product of decisions made years ago. It is one thing to keep existing projects moving, but turbulence in the relationship could make new initiatives a heavier lift.”
If India is serious about making its ambition to be a global powerhouse a reality, Vaishnav thinks there’s a clearcut way to win. “I would argue that the most important investment is political – ensuring India remains a robust, inclusive, participatory democracy,” he says. “On the economic front, India has made massive new investments in physical and digital infrastructure. But the returns on those investments will be limited unless the government doubles down on reforms: more efficient dispute resolution, an impartial legal system, even-handed tax enforcementand regulatory certainty.”
Ultimately, neither side can afford to treat the other as expendable. The test now is whether strategic foundations can hold at a time of global political upheaval.

Vibe check
Prarthna Singh has consistently placed the female identity at the heart of her artistic practice, documenting Indian women’s aspirations and acts of rebellion in male-dominated spaces. When commissioned to photograph rkivecity’s menswear line, made from discarded clothes reworked into new garments, she turned that same gaze outward. The setting was the acclaimed 151-year-old Mayo College boys’ school in Ajmer, Rajasthan – Singh attended the linked girls’ school, and credits it with shaping her rebellious spirit.
“I was thinking about how I could bring a sense of intimacy and camaraderie of boarding-school life to the images, because that exists,” she told me. One image shows a pair of hands holding another boy’s jacket, the faces left out of the frame, so the garment stands in for the familiarity they share. Seeing this work against the backdrop of students taking to the streets to fight for their rights lends the series a lasting significance. “This was just my way of showing all of this is connected. These worlds are not existing separately,” said Singh.

Mention the online apps available as part of Google Workspace, and most people will immediately think of Google Drive, Gmail, Google Docs, Google Sheets, and Google Slides—those speedy, lightweight office apps that let you get work done from any browser tab.
There's more to the suite of Google Workspace tools than you might have realized though, including an online video editing package called Google Vids. Originally launched in 2024 for business and enterprise users, the app was made available to individuals in 2026 and continues to get regular updates from Google.
Since it's both free to use and designed to run in a web browser, it's not capable of pro-level, high-resolution, multitrack video editing. But for personal and hobbyist use, it works well, and it won't take you long to learn the basics.
The Google Vids Interface
Finding Google Vids isn't difficult: You can either open Google Drive on the web, then click New and Google Vids, or head straight to the Google Vids app page and click the + (plus) button under Start a new video. (Any videos you've previously made are shown here, too.)
Besides beginning with a clean state (the Blank vid option), there are plenty of other ways to get started: You can generate AI videos with the Veo 3.1 model, turn a slideshow into a video, work from a template, upload an existing video as a starting point, create an AI music track, record a video using your camera, produce a video with an AI avatar, or create a storyboard outline. Note you can also pick the video orientation at the top.
Most of these options use a similar layout, and we're going to focus on the traditional video-making approach here—though the AI options are well worth exploring, too, if you don't have source material to work with. If you're new to Google Vids, then picking Templates from the opening splash screen will ease you in gently.
When it comes to picking a template, the topic isn't as important as the layout. Look for something that matches what you want to create as closely as possible (hover over any of the thumbnails to see an animated preview). The next dialog lets you choose whether you want to use the entire template or just selected scenes. After that, you're into the video editing interface proper.
Most of the elements should be relatively familiar if you've ever used a timeline-based video editor in the past. At the bottom you've got your video and audio tracks, while the main window shows the currently selected segment of your video. The panel on the right lets you edit whatever's currently selected.
Down the right side of the interface you've got all the options for loading in new content. You can record webcam clips, create AI videos, import footage from Google Drive and Google Photos, add voiceovers, and drop in text, images, music, and shapes. If you've started with a template, some of these elements will be styled to match.
Along the top of the Google Vids interface are more editing and formatting tools. These menus are where you should head to change transitions between scenes, to manage how elements are arranged in a particular scene, to drop in new scenes, and to manage your video project as a whole.
Building Video Projects With Google Vids
To begin building your projects, you'll probably want to load in audio, video, and images via the buttons on the right. On the most basic level, you can click the + (plus) button on the timeline to create a new scene, then drag in a photo or video from the right-hand panel to fill the scene you've just created.
A whole host of options present themselves when you right-click on the timeline. You can, for example, mute the audio track imported with a video, then add a voiceover or some different music. You're also able to split scenes (if you only want to keep half a scene maybe) and duplicate scenes (for quickly expanding the running time of your project) with a right-click.
Keep your eye on the panel on the right, which changes depending on the context. With audio tracks, you can apply fades, and with video clips you can choose from different transitions. If your scene has several elements (like shapes that scroll over a video), you're able to adjust how they look and behave.
Let's say you have a video scene and want to put some text over it. Select the scene in the timeline, click the Text button on the right, then click Add a title to do just that. If you then select the title in the scene itself, you can change the text and its styling.
Using the handles around the text box you can change its position, size, and rotation. There are also three buttons underneath on a floating toolbar: Animation lets you animate the text, Resize will resize the text box to fit the text you've entered, and Format options brings up a panel where you can change text size, padding, rotation, and so on.
Click and drag on elements inside a scene to reposition them, and right-click for more options—including Cut, Copy, Paste, and Delete. If you need more material to work with, choose the Stock option on the right, which gives you a library of material you can make use of in addition to your own content and anything created with AI.
There's a lot more to Google Vids, but that should be enough to get you started—try experimenting with a few of the templates to see what else is possible. As with the other Google Drive apps, all your edits are saved instantly, and up in the top right corner you've got a Play button for viewing your work in progress, and a Share button for when it’s ready for the world to see.
